newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IDBI bond issue to open on Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: India's IDBI bond issue to open on Jan 2.

text.p: The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) will launch its second public issue of bonds on January 2, 1997, the bank said in a statement on Wednesday.
The size of the issue will be 7.5 billion rupees with a greenshoe option of a further 7.5 billion, it said.
Four types of bond will be on offer.
The IDBI Super Deposit Bond '97 will require a minimum investment of 5,000 rupees with additional investments in multiples of 1,000 rupees each.

The bond has a maturity of eight years. Investors can choose to either avail of interest at 24.5 percent per annum payable annually starting two years after the date of allotment or 15.5 percent per annum payable annually from the date of allotment.

The IDBI Double Money Bond '97 enables investors to double their investment in four years, nine and a half months or quadruple in nine years and seven months. The minimum investment is 5,000 rupees and in multiples of 1,000 thereafter. If the Bond is sold before maturity, the difference between the sale proceeds and the issue price will be treated as capital gains, IDBI said.

The IDBI Monthly Income Bond '97, with a maturity of eight years, offers investors interest at 15 percent per annum payable monthly. In the case of early withdrawal, before maturity of the scheme, interest would be computed at 11.5 percent per annum during the second year and 13 percent during the third year. Encashments after three years will be made at face value. Encashments up to 100,000 will be made per investor per annum.
The IDBI Deep Discount Bond '97, issued at a face value of 5,500 rupees, has a maturity value of 200,000 rupees after 25 years. Investors have the facility to redeem the bonds earlier.

IDBI said if the deep discount bond is sold before maturity, the difference between the sale proceeds and the issue price would be treated as capital gains. However, if it is redeemed with IDBI, the difference between the redemption value and the issue price will be taxed as interest and will be subject to deduction of tax at source as applicable.
IDBI said it had made arrangements for market-making to provide continuous liquidity.

DSP Financial Consultants Ltd., Enam Securities Ltd., JM Share& STock Brokers Ltd., and Kotak Mahindra Capital Company will be the initial market makers, it said. They would provide two-way quotes and will be sanctioned a line of credit from IDBI for the purpose of market-making, it added.
